title: Pearl Harbor: The Morning That Changed the World
narrativeQuestion: How did decisions across the Pacific converge on one morning, and what did that morning change?

chapters.title: A Pacific on the Edge
chapters.claim: Start in China. The road to Pearl Harbor ran through a war already four years old.

chapters.title: The Admiral’s Gamble
chapters.claim: Japan’s naval leaders wanted enough time to take territory in the south. They were betting that damaging a fleet could change what a nation chose to do.

namedPeople.name: Mitsuo Fuchida
namedPeople.visualAnchorNote: Uses a clearly described period setting image.

chapters.title: Sunday Morning
chapters.claim: The fleet is in port. Alongside it, Oʻahu is waking up.

chapters.title: The Warnings
chapters.claim: A periscope near the harbor. A mass of marks on a radar screen. Two chains of information.

chapters.title: 7:55 AM
chapters.claim: By the time the first blows reached Pearl Harbor, aircraft were already attacking elsewhere on Oʻahu.

chapters.title: Battleship Row
chapters.claim: Read the moorings like a diagram. The distance from one hull to the next changed what everyone on board experienced.

chapters.title: Across the Island
chapters.claim: The name ‘Pearl Harbor’ can make the attack sound as if it happened at a single site.

chapters.title: The Second Wave
chapters.claim: A short lull gave way to more aircraft. People on the ground had already been making decisions for nearly an hour.

chapters.title: What Wasn’t Destroyed
chapters.claim: A devastated harbor could still support a fleet. That distinction shaped what happened next.

chapters.title: December 8
chapters.claim: The day after the attack, the president asked Congress for a declaration of war.

chapters.title: The Human Cost
chapters.claim: A total can describe the scale of the attack. Names and records tell us whose lives changed.

chapters.title: The World After Pearl Harbor
chapters.claim: What did one morning decide, and what remained open?
